name: InfiniGen: Efficient Generative Inference of Large Language Models with Dynamic KV Cache Management
problem: In offloading-based serving, fetching the KV cache from host memory stalls the compute core; fetching all of it wastes bandwidth that only a few entries would have used.
mechanism: Speculative KV PREFETCH: use the current layer's inputs plus PART of the next layer's query weight and key cache to do a MINIMAL REHEARSAL that predicts which few tokens the next attention layer will need, then prefetch only those KV entries from host memory. The prediction is deliberately approximate and cheap; the point is that the compute core stays busy instead of waiting on a bulk fetch.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract): improves the overall performance of a modern OFFLOADING-BASED system by UP TO 3.00x compared to prior KV cache management methods, while offering substantially better model accuracy. Baseline class is named (prior KV-management methods on an offloading system). COMPRESSION RATIO: none - this moves bytes, it does not shrink them. QUALITY COST: 'substantially better accuracy' is a relative claim; unlike KIVI/KVQuant this method never quantizes, so there is no quality-vs-bits tradeoff to report.
notes:
arXiv ID 2406.19707 verified via /abs/. Venue OSDI 2024 confirmed by the arXiv comment field ('OSDI 2024') and Semantic Scholar; year = venue year 2024.
